subject: health
topic: The 'Clean' Diet may be causing a systemic nutrient deficiency
angle: While plant-based diets are associated with micronutrient deficits due to predominant anti-nutritional factors, specific processing methods and food combinations can improve the bioavailability of these nutrients.
title: The Bioavailability Barrier

hooks.text: Are you absorbing what you eat?
You eat clean plants. Your body may still be hungry.
Your plant-based diet has a hidden barrier.
A bowl of cereal on a kitchen table.

reveal.headline: Plant foods contain components that inhibit nutrient absorption.
reveal.body: Factors like phytate, tannins, and oxalates can compromise how your body takes in essential micronutrients. This evidence is mixed regarding long-term effects.

explain.headline: The chemistry of a plant-based diet.
explain.body: Predominantly vegetarian diets are composed of components that inhibit mineral bioavailability. While processing can reduce these factors, it can also leach out minerals.

matters.headline: What your meal actually provides.
matters.body: You might be eating nutrient-dense foods that your body cannot fully access. That may be why specific culinary combinations and processing methods are necessary to improve bioavailability.

example.headline: A morning bowl of cereal.
example.body: You pour milk over toasted grains. You assume your body is absorbing the iron and calcium from the bowl. The chemistry of the grain may be preventing that.

verdict: The evidence shows that plant-based diets face significant bioavailability challenges from anti-nutrients, but these can be mitigated through specific processing and culinary combinations.
caveat: The sources do not provide specific data on the long-term physiological decline of individuals on modern 'clean' diets.
caption:
The 'clean' diet may contain hidden barriers to nutrition. 

Research shows that plant-based diets are often high in anti-nutritional factors like phytates and oxalates that inhibit mineral bioavailability. While processing can help, it can also leach out minerals. The research does not provide data on long-term physiological decline.
